  THRU:  Joseph Colombo, Director of Community Develo  t

  FROM:  Kevin Nguyen, Associate Planner II

  SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 2019-019 FOR CASE NO. PLNG2019-0081DRB -
  A REQUEST TO APPROVE THE ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN OF A
  PROPOSED SINGLE-FAMILY DWELLING ON PROPERTY LOCATED
  AT 22406 CLARKDALE AVENUE, CITY OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS

  DATE:  October 23, 2019

BACKGROUND

 The subject site is a 4,628 square foot parcel that is located on the northeast corner of
 Clarkdale Avenue and 226 th Street. The site is zoned R-2 (Medium Density Residential)
 with a General Plan Land Use Designation of "Medium Density". Surrounding land uses
•include all single-family homes to the north, south, east and west.

Under Case PLNG2019-0081 DRB, the applicant is proposing a new two-story single-
family residence with an attached two-car garage. Upon completion, the new home will
include four bedrooms and three bathrooms, and a total of approximately 2,336 square
feet of living space. The project either meets or exceeds the minimum requirements for
a proposed residential development in the R-2 zone.

DISCUSSION/ANALYSIS

Per Section 18.100.010.C of the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code (HGMC) the
approval authority for site plan review lies with the Director of Community Development.
Due to the fact that the proposal is a completely new build, the Director has decided to
refer the design review portion of the project to the Planning Commission. The Director
will still have final approval of the site plan.

It is Staff's intent that the Planning Commission focus and consider only the exterior
architecture of the proposed building, including but not limited to colors and materials,
overall architectural design, and the bulk and massing of the building. It should be
noted that there still may be some outstanding corrections required prior to final site
plan approval and the issuance of a building permit.
   P.2
 Architecture

As the plans indicate, the proposed residence encompasses a spanish design theme,
with earth-tone color for the body (Napery - Sherwin Williams), Grounded (brown) color
for roof fascia, window trim, and balcony railing. The use of Valencia eagle light tile
roofing, cultured stone veneer and decorative railing will provide articulation to the
building facade. The design takes into consideration a reduction in bulk and massing of
the building first by off-setting the garage doors to suit the angled corner lot, and
including a large decorative balcony above the garage. Additionally, a covered front
porch at the primary entryway provides variation in the front and street side elevations,
while also off-setting the various rooflines for distinction, breaking up the blank wall
between the first and second floor.

Other .architectural treatments include square columns at the front porch and second
floor balcony, decorative window trim with color contrasts, and a decorative entry door
with arched window above. The use of exposed rafter tails under the eaves will help
direct water away from the walls and the foundation.

The landscape plan will encompass new landscape throughout the property to include
trees, shrubs, and other plants, and provides an 875 square foot landscaped easement
to the City. It should be noted that the final landscape plan will be refined further prior to
permit issuance.

Staff has worked with the project architect to come up with a design that is compatible
with the surrounding area, and is compliant with the design requirements of the HGMC.
Staff believes that the design is compatible with the City's design guidelines.

DESIGN GUIDELINES

The Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code provides for broad discretion regarding the
architectural look of commercial and residential buildings under the site plan approval
process. Specifically Section 18.100.030(F)(2) of the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code
(HGMC) provides the following:

The Community Development Director and Planning Commission may also consider
and take into account the exterior architectural design, general exterior appearance,
landscaping, texture of surface materials and exterior construction, shape and bulk, and
other physical characteristics, including the location and type of public utility facilities;
and if it is found that the proposed site plan, including the considerations enumerated,
would interfere with the orderly development of the City, such site plan shall be rejected
or shall be modified or conditioned before approval so as to remove such objections.
These changes may include: a revised site plan, reduced building height, bulk or mass,
increased setbacks, changes in building materials, changes in roof lines, increased
usable open space, increased screening of garages, trash receptacles, mechanical
equipment, etc., increased landscaping, change in color or any other changes or
additions that the City feels necessary to further the goals of the site plan review
process.
   P.3
In addition, Section 18.50.100 of the HGMC indicates that design guidelines have been
developed to promote high quality development, protect the City from the adverse
effects of poor design, encourage originality, creativity, and compatibility within
neighborhoods, and to enhance the beauty, livability and prosperity of the community.

The proposal is in compliance with the design guidelines (General Provisions - HGMC
Section 18.50.100.B) as follows:

There are numerous General Provisions in the HGMC pertaining to design. Many of
these provisions are required as part of the plan checking process and are not related to
the architecture of the building. The following are the general provisions of which Staff
believes the proposed project is consistent as related to the design of the building:

  General Provision Number 1: Developmeritshall oe compatiole Witnthe character of
  the neighborhood and surrounding sites and shall not be detrimental to the orderly
  and harmonious development of the surrounding areas and of the City. The height
  and bulk of any proposed building and structure on site shall be in scale and
  proportion with surrounding structures and not dominate the site or neighborhood.
  The design of all buildings shall be of conventional wood or metal frame construction
  meeting industry standards. The exterior finish shall not have exposed rough lumber
  and shall have a minimum of a stucco application, wood siding, or similar material.

  •  The design encompasses traditional design elements, including stucco, cultured
  stone veneer, window accents, and eagle light tile roof. The overall appearance
  takes massing into consideration by pushing part of the second story back, off-
  setting the rooflines as well as the garage doors, and the addition of a small
  covered porch at the main entrance, thus creating a welcoming aesthetic for the
  front faqade.

  General Provision Number 7: Building elevations, design characteristics and other
  architectural and aesthetic features shall not be unsightly, undesirable, or obnoxious
  in appearance; shall create an orderly and aesthetically pleasing environment; and
  shall be harmonious and compatible with existing development in the area.

  •  The building elevation creates a Spanish architectural far;ade, avoiding modern
  architectural elements and thus, blending with the traditional homes in the City of
  Hawaiian Gardens. The welcoming entry porch with traditional elements, off-set
  rooflines, and exposed rafter tails will help to achieve an aesthetically pleasing
  environment along Clarkdale and 226th frontages.

  General Provision Number 8: New development and remodeling shall be designed
  in such a way to upgrade the appearance of the area.

  •  The finished home will present a new residence on a lot that has been vacant for
  some time, thus upgrading this section of Clarkdale Avenue.

  General Provision Number 13: New development shall incorporate clay or concrete
  roof tile. In addition, all exterior colors painted on the surface of the building,
  including stucco, shall be an earth tone color including off-whites and creams.
   P.4

  •  The colors and materials are earth tone in nature including beige (Napery) and
  brown (Grounded}, with tile roofing designed to look like traditional mission style
  roofing to match the overall architecture presented for the new home.

Design Standards and Guidelines (HGMC18.50.100.C):

  Guideline Number 1: In addition to the height and setback requirements for each
  zone, changes in material, height, projections in the vertical and horizontal plane or
  similar fai;;ade changes are required on visible exterior walls.

  •  The proposed dwelling includes numerous offset planes with changes in
  rooflines, pushing back part of the first and second story of the building, and the
  inclusion of a large balcony above the garage, as well as a smaller covered front
  porch to provide a variation in the vertical and horizontal planes. Changes in
  building material including cultured stone, smooth stucco, and decorative railing
  are also included in the proposal.

Staff believes that the proposed dwelling provides for an architecturally pleasing
development, involving a traditional looking home that is well balanced and provides an
upgrade to the overall streetscape along Clarkdale Avenue and 226 1h Street.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

Staff has reviewed the proposed project for compliance with the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Upon completion of this review, staff determined
thatthis request is categorically exempt from CEQA, pursuant to Guideline Section No.
15303 (Class 3, New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures). Categorical
Exemptions are projects, which have been determined not to have a significant effect on
the environment and have been exempted from the requirements of the California
Environmental Quality Act. Class 3 includes construction of new structure including this
request. It is staff's opinion the proposed residential dwelling will not have a significant
effect on the environment; thereby qualifying for the Class 3 exemption.

CONCLUSION

Staff finds that the new development meets the design criteria of the City of Hawaiian
Gardens and recommends that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. 2019-
019, approving Case Number PLNG2019-0081 DRB.

  SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 2019-020 FOR CASE NO. PLNG2019-0072DRB -
  A REQUEST TO APPROVE THE ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN OF A
  SECOND RESIDENTIAL DWELLING AND A NEW 4-CAR GARAGE,
  ON PROPERTY LOCATED AT 21826 CLARKDALE AVENUE, CITY
  OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS

  DATE:  October 23, 2019

BACKGROUND

The subject site is a 5,331 square foot parcel that is located on the northeast corner of
Clarkdale Avenue and Civic Center Drive. The site is zoned R-2 (Medium Density
Residential) with a General Plan Land Use Designation of "Medium Density".
Surrounding land uses include all single-family homes to the north, south, east and
west.

Under Case PLNG2019-0072DRB, the applicant is proposing a second residential
dwelling localed above a new 4-car garage. The new 1,420 square foot residence and
garage will be attached to rear of the existing primary residence. Upon completion, the
new unit will include three bedrooms, one-half bathrooms, and 80 square feet of private
balcony. The project either meets or exceeds the minimum requirements for a proposed
residential development in the R-2 zone.

DISCUSSION/ANALYSIS

Per Section 18.100.01 0.C of the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code (HGMC) the
approval authority for site plan review lies with the Director of Community Development.
Due to the fact that the proposal is a completely new build, the Director has decided to
refer the design review portion of the project to the Planning Commission. The Director
will still have final approval of the site plan.

It is Staff's intent that the Planning Commission focus and consider only the exterior
architecture of the proposed building, including but not limited to colors and materials,
overall architectural design, and the bulk and massing of the building. It should be
   P. 16
 noted that there still may be some outstanding corrections required prior to final site
 plan approval and the issuance of a building permit.

 Architecture

As the plans indicate, the proposed residence encompasses a traditional design theme,
with the combination of stucco finish in sand color (Snowy Pine - Behr) and horizontal
siding (Back to Nature - Behr) for the body, new shingle roof, window trim (Brass Button
-Behr), and horizontal siding along the bottom of building to provide articulation to the
facade. The design takes into consideration a reduction in bulk and massing of the
building first by off-setting the balcony above the garage and entryway to provide
variation along the street side elevation, while also off-setting the various rooflines for
distinction, breaking up the blank wall on the second floor.

Other architectural treatments include decorative window trim with color contrasts and a
decorative railing for the balcony above. The applicant is planning to upgrade the
existing primary residence by painting the structure and using same architectural
elements with colors and materials that match the proposed second unit.

Staff has worked with the project architect to come up with a design that is compatible
with the surrounding area, and is compliant with the design requirements of the HGMC.
Staff believes that the design is compatible with the City's design guidelines.

DESIGN GUIDELINES

The Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code provides for broad discretion regarding the
architectural look of commercial and residential buildings under the site plan approval
process. Specifically, Section 18.100.030(F)(2) of the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal
Code (HGMC) provides the following:

The Community Development Director and Planning Commission may also consider
and take into account the exterior architectural design, general exterior appearance,
landscaping, texture of surface materials and exterior construction, shape and bulk, and
other physical characteristics, including the location and type of public utility facilities;
and if it is found that the proposed site plan, including the considerations enumerated,
would interfere with the orderly development of the City, such site plan shall be rejected
or shall be modified or conditioned before approval so as to remove such objections.
   P. 1 7
These changes may include: a revised site plan, reduced building height, bulk or mass,
increased setbacks, changes in building materials, changes in roof lines, increased
usable open space, mechanical equipment, etc., increased landscaping, change in color
or any other changes or additions that the City feels necessary to further the goals of
the site plan review process.

In addition, Section 18.50.100 of the HGMC indicates that design guidelines have been
developed to promote high quality development, protect the City from the adverse
effects of poor design, encourage originality, creativity, and compatibility within
neighborhoods, and to enhance the beauty, livability and prosperity of the community.

The proposal is complying with the design guidelines (General Provisions - HGMC
Section 18.50.100.B) as follows:

There are numerous General Provisions in the HGMC pertaining to design. Many of
these provisions are required as part of the plan checking process and are not related to
the architecture of the building. The following are the general provisions of which Staff
believes the proposed project is consistent as related to the design of the building:

  General Provision Number 1: Development shall be compatible with the character of
  the neighborhood and surrounding sites and shall not be detrimental to the orderly
  and harmonious development of the surrounding areas and of the City. The height
  and bulk of any proposed building and structure on site shall be in scale and
  proportion with surrounding structures and not dominate the site or neighborhood.
  The design of all buildings shall be of conventional wood or metal frame construction
  meeting industry standards. The exterior finish shall not have exposed rough lumber
  and shall have a minimum of a stucco application, wood siding, or similar material.

  •  The design encompasses traditional design elements, including stucco, wood
  siding, window accents, and shingle composition roof. The overall appearance
  takes massing into consideration by pushing part of the second story back, off-
  setting the roof!ines as well as the garage doors, and the addition of a small
  covered porch at the main entrance, thus creating a welcoming aesthetic for the
  front far;ade.

  General Provision Number 7: Building elevations, design characteristics and other
  architectural and aesthetic features shall not be unsightly, undesirable, or obnoxious
  in appearance; shall create an orderly and aesthetically pleasing environment; and
  shall be harmonious and compatible with existing development in the area.

  •  The building elevation creates a Spanish architectural far;ade, avoiding modern
  architectural elements and thus, blending with the traditional homes in the City of
  Hawaiian Gardens. The welcoming entry porch with traditional elements, off-set
  roof/ines, and exposed rafter tails will help to achieve an aesthetically pleasing
  environment along Clarkdale and Civic Center frontages.

  General Provision Number 8: New development and remodeling shall be designed
  in such a way to upgrade the appearance of the area.
   P. 18
  •  The finished home will add a second unit and upgrade the appearance of the
  existing structure, thus upgrading this section of Clarkdale Avenue.

  General Provision Number 13: New development shall incorporate clay or concrete
  roof tile. In addition, all exterior colors painted on the surface of the building,
  including stucco, shall be an earth tone color including off-whites and creams.

  •  The colors and materials are nature colors including sand (Snowy Pine), Back to
  Nature and Brass Button, with shingle composition roofing designed to look like
  traditional style roofing to match with the color and material of the existing house.

Design Standards and Guidelines (HGMC18.50.100.C):

  Guideline Number 1: In addition to the height and setback requirements for each
  zone, changes in material, height, projections in the vertical and horizontal plane or
  similar fai;:ade changes are required on visible exterior walls.  ·

  •  The proposed second unit and garage include numerous offset planes witl)
  changes in rooflines, pushing back part of the first and second story of the
  building, and the inclusion of a large balcony above the garage, as well as a
  smaller covered front porch to provide a variation in the vertical and horizontal
  planes. Changes in building material including cultured stone, smooth stucco,
  and decorative railing are also included in the proposal.

Staff believes that the proposed dwelling provides for an architecturally pleasing
development, involving a traditional looking home that is well balanced and provides an
upgrade to the overall streetscape along Clarkdale Avenue and Civic Center Drive.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

Staff has reviewed the proposed project for compliance with the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Upon completion of this review, staff determined
that this request is categorically exempt from CEQA, pursuant to Guideline Section No.
15303 (Class 3, New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures). Categorical
Exemptions are projects, which have been determined not to have a significant effect on
the environment and have been exempted from the requirements of the California
Environmental Quality Act. Class 3 includes construction of new structure including this
request. 11 is staff's opinion the proposed residential dwelling will not have a significant
effect on the environment; thereby qualifying for the Class 3 exemption.

CONCLUSION

Staff finds that the new development meets the design criteria of the City of Hawaiian
Gardens and recommends that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. 2019-
020, approving Case Number PLNG2019-0072DRB.

  DATE:  October 23, 2019

BACKGROUND

The Planning Division as part of the Community Development Department is
responsible for the implementation of the policies and objectives of the community as
set forth in the City of Hawaiian Gardens General Plan and Zoning Ordinance. The
City's Planning Division guides the City's orderly development, thus achieving a livable
city that balances the needs of residents and businesses. Current planning projects
range from residential additions to new commercial developments. Staff serves the
Planning Commission by providing reports and detailed analysis for projects subject to
discretionary review.

At the regular meeting of the Planning Commission on October 9, 2019, a request was
made to present a status report of planning projects previously approved by the
Planning Commission. The attached list is a summary of all projects that have been
approved in the past 12 months, October 2018 through October 2019, and provides
additional details as to the final status of these projects.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission of the City of Hawaiian Gardens
receive and file the Planning Division status report.
